summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with strong embedded software and microcontroller firmware experience across STM32, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson. Writes bare-metal embedded C and embedded C++ under real-time constraints, with interrupt-driven designs, UART/I2C/SPI drivers, PWM motor control, and closed-loop feedback on moving hardware, and builds for clean code and modular architecture.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a metal surface inspection pipeline combining custom image stitching, wavelet denoising, and depth estimation; raised stitching quality from PSNR 65 to 86.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Took over as team lead mid-project on a cross-cultural team of 7, restructuring task distribution to deliver the full pipeline within the 6-week window.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal embedded C on STM32 (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM and a deterministic 1 Hz rate.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override, driven by YOLOv8 detections sent from NVIDIA Jetson to STM32 over UART.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Robocon Robot - Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Built closed-loop heading correction in embedded C++ on Arduino Due, feeding angular error from quadrature encoder odometry (2400 CPR) back into rotation PWM to hold course.
Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding as a 4-bit A/B state machine, drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM, and added a fail-safe halting all motors on controller disconnect.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system across a three-layer distributed pipeline on a unified WebSocket fabric, with two-link inverse kinematics in embedded C++ on Arduino.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale frames) to reach 100% pick reliability over 10 trials; deployed the Jetson bridge as a systemd service.
